units.u: number_of_units summed over the block's parcel rows. NOT A COUNT OF HOMES and not shown as one: the roll reads 0 on every CONDOMINIUM parcel, because there the parcel IS the home — 155,111 Single Family Residential rows carry 121,707 units between them city-wide, and block 0311 reads 11 against the Census's 76. Carried as evidence, and the panel reads `hu`.
units.v: assessed value, THOUSANDS of USD — land + improvements + fixtures
units.ar: built floor area, HUNDREDS of square feet
units.us: index into useNames — the roll's OWN use_definition, verbatim, for the use the most parcels here are on; -1 where the roll gives this block no parcel
units.pop: 2020 Census residents; -1 where no census ring resolved here
units.hu: 2020 Census housing units (HU100), the count the panel shows as homes; -1 where no census ring resolved here. 406,628 city-wide, which is the published county total.

roll.name: Assessor Historical Secured Property Tax Rolls
roll.publisher: City & County of San Francisco (Office of the Assessor-Recorder)
roll.licence: DataSF open data — Open Data Commons PDDL
roll.what: the closed secured roll. `block` is the assessor block, so a block figure is the sum over that block's own published parcel rows.

parcels.name: Parcels – Active and Retired
parcels.publisher: City & County of San Francisco (Department of Public Works)
parcels.licence: DataSF open data — Open Data Commons PDDL
parcels.what: the parcel base map. The active parcels are the same file the map's own block rings were dissolved from (manifest.sources.blocks); their published centroids are what carries a census block onto an assessor block here.

census.name: 2020 Census Redistricting Data (P.L. 94-171), block level
census.licence: work of the US government, public domain
census.what: POP100 and HU100 — the 2020 Census count — on the Census Bureau's own block rings. 5,986 rings in San Francisco County summing to 873,965 residents, which is the published county total.

not_measured: The assessed value is what the closed roll carries, which is Proposition 13 base year value and not a market price; a parcel that has not changed hands since 1978 is on the roll at its 1978 value plus the allowed annual increase. The census count is the 2020 count on the Census Bureau's own block, carried onto the assessor block holding most of that ring's parcels — it is not a count of this block.
